newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, April up but off high.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, April up but off high.

text.p: Late liquidation erased much of the midday gain in April CME live cattle futures at the close while other months ended mostly lower, traders said. Sharp gains posted earlier in the day in the feeder cattle pit also faded by the close, but prices ended mostly higher.

Live cattle closed 0.225 cent a lb lower to 0.150 higher with April up 0.125 at 68.825 cents after earlier rising to 69.700 cents. Feeders ended 0.050 cent a lb lower to 0.775 higher with May up 0.475 at 68.925 cents.
Late liquidation by commercials and locals who had been buyers early, weighed on live cattle late, sources said.

April live cattle had rallied to 1-1/2 week highs on talk of packers raising bids and paying $68 per cwt for cash cattle. Packers need cattle and feedlots are current which will keep fed markets firm, traders said.

"Feedlots are so current they are running 20 lbs a head below a year ago on the fed cattle weights so they have very little pressure to move animals," said Jim Robb, economist with the Livestock Marketing Information Center.
But Robb noted that as beef prices have eased, packer margins have been squeezed to the point that packers have been buying cattle on a hand-to-mouth basis.
The heavy-weight choice boxed beef value fell another $1.42 per cwt at noon to $103.24, down $4.55 in the past week.
R.J. O'Brien sold at the close after buying on the rally along with ADM Investor Services. Cargill Investor Services sold April early, pit sources said.
Traders cited expectations on Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report for some of the pressure in back months as the report is expected to show large on-feed supplies.
Analysts' estimates ranged from 105 to 107.5 percent of a year ago for on-feed supplies at larger feedlots in the seven major states as of March 1 and averaged 106.5 percent.
February placements averaged 104.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 99 to 110 percent and marketings averaged 97.9 in a a range of 94 to 99 percent.
In live cattle options, there was selling of April 70 calls on the rally which took volatility down 1/2 to one percent. Call selling persisted in April late despite the setback, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures retreated along with live cattle late and lightly-traded March slipped below Tuesday's close for a closing loss. Feeders had been supported most of the day by lower corn futures, traders said.
Corn fell as much as the daily limit after feeder cattle futures closed, which prompted early calls for feeders to open higher again Thursday, traders added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.08 at $68.69 per cwt.

Selling by RBH and market-on-close orders partly offset buying by ADM late. Refco and Dean Witter bought May early while LFG sold, traders said and Cargill spread long August live cattle/short April feeders and long February live cattle/short October feeders early.
